punchline: During the tensest days of the Cuban Missile Crisis, Kennedy sat in meetings drawing two sailboats on a yellow legal pad.
thirty_sec: October 1962: Soviet missile sites turn up in Cuba, and Kennedy's advisors want an airstrike and an invasion. He'd already been pushed into the Bay of Pigs, and he'd just read a book about leaders stumbling into World War One. So he slowed everyone down, asked why the Soviets did it, and chose a blockade he called a 'quarantine.' Eleven days in, Khrushchev wrote about a knot of war and backed off.
